summary: Console login intermittently fails for internal tools due to Okta composite-hash attribute mismatch
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC several internal users report being unable to sign in to multiple internal consoles (support-portal, model-insights, runbook-editor). The failure correlates with an Okta assertion containing a newly-introduced composite attribute used by an upstream HR sync job. Impact: ~12% of interactive console logins in us-west are failing with 401/403 or dropping to a zero-length session after SSO redirect. This affects oncall and developer productivity; escalated to P1. Observed behavior: Users are redirected back to the login page with no UI error, or receive 403 with "identity.claim_validation_failed" in logs. Okta SAML/ OIDC assertions appear to have an additional attribute key: "x-composite-hash" that sometimes exceeds expected length causing the identity-service claim normalizer to truncate and produce a mismatched composite hash claim. Expected behavior: Identity proxy consumes Okta assertions, normalizes claims, and issues internal session tokens consistently regardless of optional composite attributes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a user account where Okta profile has recently been updated via HR sync (examples in investigation notes).
2) Navigate to https://support.redwood.internal and click Sign in -> SSO (Okta),
3) Complete Okta login flow and return to Redwood auth-proxy,
4) Observe either immediate redirect back to /login (no error) or 403 response in network tab with body 'identity.claim_validation_failed'.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Ethan Cole: Replayed assertion from affected user; raw assertion includes 'x-composite-hash' > 900 chars. Our normalizer truncates trailing chars and recomputes composite; mismatch triggers session rejection.

2026-03-10 10:20 - Identity Eng (S. Müller): HR sync introduced composite attribute to encode multiple legacy group IDs; Okta team rolled this without notifying us. The attribute sometimes contains non-ASCII separators which our claim parser removes causing different hash values.
2026-03-11 14:40 - Support: Noted spike in 401s at 08:30 UTC; other regions not affected because HR sync targets us-west only for initial rollout.
2026-03-12 11:15 - Ethan Cole: Crafted a dev patch to relax strict length check and preserve non-ASCII separators in parsing logic; tests show successful round-trip for sample assertions.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Multiple oncall engineers hit this during shift change; temporary workaround requested to allow manual session creation for affected users.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Liam O'Connor (Platform): Suggested short-term mitigation: add a normalization flag to identity-proxy to bypass composite-hash verification for assertions containing x-composite-hash > 256 until patch is deployed.

2026-03-12 16:45 - Ethan Cole (assignee): Deployed bypass toggle to prod auth-proxy in us-west (feature-flag 'relax-composite-hash-check' = true). Verified login success for 40/40 previously failing accounts; monitoring.
2026-03-13 08:00 - Priya Ramesh (reporter): Confirmed oncall can authenticate; please document follow-up and permanent fix timeline.
root_cause_hypothesis: Upstream HR sync added a large composite attribute (x-composite-hash) containing non-ASCII separators. Our claim_normalizer truncates/strips those separators before hashing, causing calculated hash != hash provided by the assertion, leading to session rejection.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: feature-flagged bypass deployed to auth-proxy in us-west to allow user logins while identity-service patch (PR 872) normalizes parsing to preserve separators and safely compute hash for arbitrarily long composite attributes. Full rollout scheduled after security review. Follow-ups: 1) Security to review bypass risk and approve exception window. 2) Deploy PR 872 to prod and revert bypass flag. 3) Add unit test for non-ASCII separators and long attributes.
